summary: Gives three distribution lists for network documents: list A for sites sending their own documents, and lists B and C for the Network Information Center to send copies to other participants. It replaces RFC 95 and RFC 155 and was replaced by RFC 211.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 168 lists postal recipients for network documents and explains which of three lists to use. It replaced RFC 95 and RFC 155, and was later replaced by RFC 211.

subtitle: Three postal mailing lists for distributing early network documents

tldr.problem: Network sites and participants needed clear mailing lists for distributing RFCs and other network documents.
tldr.mechanism: List A is for sites to send their own documents to liaisons; Lists B and C are for NIC distribution to participants and station agents.
tldr.outcome: RFC 168 superseded RFC 95 and RFC 155 and was later replaced by RFC 211.

facts.label: Station-agent mailing frequency
facts.value: Once a week or more often when quantity warrants

sections.title: Three Lists for Network Documents
sections.content:
The RFC identifies three lists for distributing network documents. Sites use List A to send their own documents to liaisons as quickly as possible; all but local mail should be sent by air mail.

The Network Information Center uses Lists B and C to distribute copies to non-site network participants and station agents. The RFC says these lists supersede RFC 95 and RFC 155.
sections.plainLanguage: Different senders use different lists. Sites send their documents to liaisons using List A, while the NIC uses Lists B and C for other participants and station agents.

sections.title: Initial Distribution to Liaisons
sections.content:
List A is the initial distribution list. It includes network liaisons and others who should receive RFCs whether the sender is the NIC or a site. These recipients also receive selected catalogs and other formal documents from the NIC.

The body of the RFC gives contact names and postal addresses for the listed sites.
sections.plainLanguage: List A names the liaisons and other contacts who should receive initial copies of RFCs and selected NIC documents.

sections.title: NIC Participants and Station Agents
sections.content:
List B names network participants who receive formal documents sent from the NIC, either when liaisons are mailed or when station agents are sent documents. List C identifies NIC station agents.

Station agents receive copies of documents distributed to liaisons and documents sent as part of a station collection. The NIC says it mails to station agents once a week, or more often when the quantity warrants.
sections.plainLanguage: List B is for other network participants. List C names station agents who receive copies and help handle local document collections.

references.text: Postel, J., "Distribution of NWG/RFC's through the NIC," RFC 95, 1971.
